correctness.rationale: The independent BSC transition matrix and constant conditional entropy are exact. Invertibility gives strict concavity over the input simplex for 0<p<1/2; output reversal/complement symmetry forces the two endpoint weights equal. The explicit second derivative is negative on the symmetric segment, while F_t′(0)>0 and F_t′(1)<0, giving a unique strictly interior optimizer and all-noise gain. At both endpoints direct channel limits resolve equality/strictness. Analytic implicit-function expansion with rational coefficient checks establishes beta=t²−3t⁴+34t⁶/3+O(t⁸), and gain=(t⁶−3t⁸+32t¹⁰/3+O(t¹²))/ln2. Saved exact fraction and high-precision checks passed; they corroborate the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The 2025 channel study numerically observes that allowing a mixed symbol seems to provide very little benefit when reads approach maximal noise. A strict theorem for every nonmaximal noise level and the sharp t⁶ coefficient identify both the structural fact that optimal signaling uses all three symbols and the quantitative mechanism for near-equality, useful when comparing ordered composite letters to repeated binary reads.
